Name: learning_rate_schedule
Title: Adaptive Learning Rate Schedules: Comparing different learning rate schedules for diffusion models.
Experiment: In this experiment, we compare the performance of different learning rate schedules on diffusion model performance. We use the final estimated KL as the evaluation metric.

Name: cfg_mode_control
Title: Controllable Generation via Classifier-Free Guidance on Discovered Modes: A Fidelity-Diversity Trade-off Study
Experiment: 1) Add a preprocessing step that runs k-means (sklearn, fixed k=4 for all datasets for consistency, or k chosen via silhouette score capped at [2,6]) on each dataset's raw 2D points to assign each point a pseudo-class label representing a spatial mode. 2) Modify MLPDenoiser to accept a label input y: add an nn.Embedding(num_classes+1, embedding_dim) (last index reserved as the 'null'/unconditional token), concatenate its output with the existing x1/x2/t embeddings before the main network. 3) Modify the training loop to pass the pseudo-label for each batch element into the model (extend dataset/DataLoader to also yield labels), replacing it with the null token with probability p=0.1-0.2 (CFG dropout). 4) Modify the sampling loop to, for a chosen guidance weight w and target label y, compute eps_cond = model(x,t,y) and eps_uncond = model(x,t,null), then use eps = eps_uncond + w*(eps_cond - eps_uncond) as the noise prediction fed into noise_scheduler.step. 5) Run sampling across a sweep of guidance weights w in {0,1,2,4,8,16} for each dataset: (a) conditioned on each individual mode label, and (b) unconditionally. 6) Evaluate primarily: per-mode fidelity (assign generated samples to nearest real-data cluster centroid and measure accuracy against intended label) and diversity (entropy over cluster assignment of unconditionally-generated samples) as functions of w, alongside the existing global KL divergence metric vs w. Optionally compute per-cluster KL for a few (dataset, w) combinations as a secondary check. Produce fidelity-vs-diversity trade-off plots per dataset.
